title: Zomunk vs MakeMyTrip vs Flight Klub Flight Finder: Which Should You Use?
excerpt: Zomunk sends deal alerts, MakeMyTrip is a booking site, and Flight Klub Flight Finder shows live fares free with no login and a human to help. Here's how the three compare and when to use each.
content:
Zomunk and MakeMyTrip get compared a lot, but they aren't really competitors. They do different jobs, and knowing which job you need can save you money.

**What Zomunk does**

Zomunk is a flight deal alert service. It watches international round-trip fares from major Indian airports and flags the unusually good ones, such as big drops and mistake fares. It is not a booking platform: it sends you to Google Flights, an airline or an OTA to buy. Free members see a limited set of economy deals, and premium unlocks the full feed.

**What MakeMyTrip does**

MakeMyTrip is an online travel agency. You search a route and date, compare fares and book on the spot, for flights, hotels and more. It shows you what's available for *your* trip, rather than a curated list of standout deals.

**The practical difference**

- **Zomunk** answers: "what's an unusually good fare right now?" That helps if you're flexible on where and when.
- **MakeMyTrip** answers: "what's available for my dates, and can I book it here?" That helps once you've decided.

Many travellers use both: an alert to spot a rare deal, and an OTA or fare board to check the price and buy.

**Flight Klub Flight Finder: live fares, free, with a human to help**

[Flight Klub Flight Finder](/flight-finder) is a public fare board. Pick your city and destination and see fares now, with no login, no subscription and no app. Where the other two split the job, this one covers both halves:

- **Search on demand**, like an OTA, from Bangalore, Delhi, Hyderabad and more, [international and domestic](/flight-finder), plus a [long weekend flights](/flight-finder) view
- **A person behind every fare.** The "Get help" button opens WhatsApp with a real Flight Klub travel expert who can add hotels, visas and a full tour package to the flight
- **Free.** There's no premium tier holding the good fares back

**How the three compare**

| | Zomunk | MakeMyTrip | Flight Klub Flight Finder |
|---|---|---|---|
| What it is | Deal alert service | Booking site | Fare board + human help |
| Search your own dates | No — curated deals | Yes | Yes |
| Books the ticket | No | Yes | Via WhatsApp, with an expert |
| Login needed | Yes | For booking | No |
| Cost | Free tier + premium | Free to search | Free |
| Plans hotels and itinerary | No | Separate booking | Yes, on request |

**Which should you use?**

- Flexible, and happy to be alerted to rare mistake fares → Zomunk
- Know your dates and just want to book yourself → MakeMyTrip
- Want to see real fares now, with someone to plan the whole trip if you like → [Flight Klub Flight Finder](/flight-finder)

If you'd like to read more, we've covered Zomunk reviews: is it worth it?, Best Zomunk Alternatives in India and Flight Klub vs Zomunk on pricing.

**Which is best: Zomunk, MakeMyTrip or Flight Klub Flight Finder?**

For most trips, Flight Klub Flight Finder is the easiest starting point: it's free, needs no login, shows live fares, and there's a real person if you want the whole trip planned. Zomunk suits deal-hunters who don't mind waiting for alerts, and MakeMyTrip suits people who want to book a known itinerary themselves.

**Is Zomunk better than MakeMyTrip?**

They solve different problems. Zomunk flags standout fares but doesn't sell tickets, while MakeMyTrip lets you search and book for your dates. Neither is strictly better. It depends on whether you're hunting for a deal or booking a planned trip.

**Can I book flights on Zomunk like on MakeMyTrip?**

No. Zomunk shows the deal and sends you to Google Flights, an airline or an OTA to book.

Mainly to enable push notifications when a new deal is found, since an account-based alert system needs somewhere to send the alert. It also limits the free tier to a small selection of deals, with the full catalogue behind a paid plan.

title: We Tested ChatGPT, Gemini & Perplexity for Trips
excerpt: A travel agent's honest breakdown of what ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity do well for trip planning, and what they still get badly wrong.
content:
**Quick answer:** AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity are useful for building skeleton itineraries and general destination research, but they fail at real-time flight pricing, current hotel availability, and India-specific logistics like visa rules for tier-2 city travelers. For a trip from India, AI gets the broad structure right but misses the details that actually make or break a booking.

Everyone in the travel industry is talking about AI. Most of what they're saying is either breathless hype or defensive dismissal. Here's something more useful: an honest test of how the three main AI tools — ChatGPT (GPT-4o), Google Gemini 1.5, and Perplexity — actually perform on real travel planning tasks.

We gave each tool the same brief: plan a 7-night trip to Thailand for a couple from Bangalore in May 2026, budget ₹1,20,000 total, mix of beach and city, no group tours.

**What does AI actually get right for India trip planning?**

All three tools produced a reasonable skeleton itinerary within seconds. Bangkok for 2 nights, then down to Koh Samui or Phuket for 5 nights — the logical structure is correct. Gemini and Perplexity both pulled live flight data and gave broadly accurate price ranges for May (₹18,000–26,000 return from BLR). ChatGPT, without browsing enabled, quoted prices from its training data that were 15–20% lower than current fares.

For general destination research — what to eat in Chiang Mai, how to get from Bangkok to Koh Samui, what the Thai visa-on-arrival process looks like — all three were excellent. Accurate, detailed, well-organised. This is the task AI does best: synthesising widely available reference information into a readable summary.

Perplexity stood out for up-to-date news. It correctly flagged that the Southern Thailand monsoon season runs May–October (so Phuket and Samui get hit), and recommended Koh Lanta or Krabi instead for a May trip — which is genuinely good advice that many people miss.

**Where does AI fail for Indian travelers?**

Hotel recommendations were the biggest weakness. Every tool recommended well-known properties — the kind that rank highly in training data. When we asked for boutique hotels on Koh Lanta under ₹6,000/night, two of the three suggested places that no longer exist or have changed ownership. ChatGPT hallucinated a hotel with a glowing description that we simply cannot find in any booking system.

Flight routing was worse than expected. Gemini recommended a routing that doesn't exist as a single booking — it combined two separate tickets (IndiGo BLR to Bangkok, then a Thai domestic carrier with no interline agreement) without flagging the risk. If the first flight is delayed, you miss the connection with no protection. A travel agent would never do this.

Visa nuance was mostly handled correctly, but with important gaps. None of the tools mentioned that Indian passport holders on a Thailand visa-on-arrival need to show proof of onward travel — a requirement that catches people at Suvarnabhumi every week.

And critically: none of them can actually book anything. They can tell you prices but cannot access live inventory, cannot hold seats, and cannot respond when things go wrong.

**Should you use AI to plan your next trip from India?**

AI is now a genuinely useful research assistant for travel. Use Perplexity to get oriented on a new destination — what to see, roughly what it costs, what the weather is doing. Use ChatGPT to brainstorm itinerary structures or compare two destinations. These are real time-savers.

But AI is not a travel agent. It cannot negotiate rates, cannot access GDS inventory, cannot spot the routing trap that ruins your connection, and cannot call the hotel at midnight when your room is wrong. The travellers who will do best in the AI era are the ones who use these tools for research and then hand the actual booking to someone who can be held accountable.

That's still us. And we're not worried.

title: How to Read a Flight Fare Board: A Practical Guide for Indian Travellers
excerpt: What a fare board shows, how to read a fare card, the traps to avoid and a simple routine for finding a cheap flight.
content:
A fare board and a search engine do different jobs. Here is how to read a fare board, what the numbers mean and the traps to avoid.

## What a fare board shows

A board lists the cheapest round-trip fare found for each destination from your city, usually with the month and airline. It answers *where can I go and when is it cheap*. A search engine answers *what does this exact trip cost on this exact day*.

## How to read a fare card

- **Price:** the round-trip fare for one adult on the dates shown.
- **Dates:** the departure and return the price applies to. Move either date and the fare can change.
- **Stops and duration:** a cheaper fare can mean a long layover. Check the flight time.
- **Airline:** baggage and meals differ between carriers.

## Traps to avoid

- **Only looking at the headline price.** It is the cheapest date pair, which may not be your dates.
- **Ignoring baggage.** A low-cost carrier fare may exclude checked bags.
- **Forgetting the rest of the trip.** Stay costs vary by month too, so compare the whole trip.
- **Treating the fare as fixed.** Airlines change prices through the day.

## A simple routine

1. Open the [Flight Klub Flight Finder](/flight-finder), choose your city and look at the month strip.
2. Pick two or three destinations and open their route pages to see the dates.
3. Check the same dates on the airline or your usual site before paying.
4. If you want flights, stays and transfers planned together, [ask Flight Klub](https://wa.me/918722936433).

## Common questions

**Why is the price at checkout different?** Airlines change prices during the day and by booking channel; a board shows what was found on its nightly check.
